# gitmoap_group_catalog_environment (Resource)

Declares an environment, a place services deploy to, that every repository beneath the group can deploy to unless it declares its own environment with the same slug. Maintainers and above may declare one; a production-tier environment needs an Owner. Unless you set its protection, a production environment requires an approval from the group's direct members before each deploy and accepts deploys from `main` only.

The token needs `catalog:manage` and `catalog:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The owning group's id
- `slug` (String)

### Optional

- `concurrency` (Attributes) Whether deploys to an environment run one at a time, and what happens to a deploy that has to
wait. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--concurrency))
- `display_name` (String)
- `protection` (Attributes) The rules for deploying to an environment: whether a deployment needs approval and from whom,
which refs may deploy, and which groups and repositories may use it. Approvers are checked when
the approval is given, so a change in who belongs to a team applies at once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protection))
- `tier` (String) What kind of environment this is, whatever it is called: `development`, `testing`, `staging`
or `production`. A `production` environment is protected by default.
- `url` (String)

### Read-Only

- `approval_enforced` (Boolean) Whether the platform enforces `protection.requires_approval` on deploys, so a client can tell
a policy that is applied from one that is only recorded.
- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the environment is archived. An archived environment can no longer be deployed to
but keeps its deployment history, and archiving can be undone. An environment with
deployments cannot be deleted, only archived.
- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `environment_id` (String) The environment's id
- `owner_full_path` (String) The full path of the group or repository that owns the environment (e.g. `acme/platform`),
which shows when an environment in a repository's listing comes from a group above it. With
the slug it forms the environment's OIDC claim, `{owner_full_path}:{slug}`.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `variable_count` (Number) How many variables the environment holds.
- `version` (Number) Increases with every change. Send it with an update to have the update refused with `409`
if someone else changed the environment first.

<a id="nestedatt--concurrency"></a>
### Nested Schema for `concurrency`

Optional:

- `exclusive` (Boolean) Whether deploys to this environment run one at a time. Off by default.
- `max_lock_wait_seconds` (Number) How long a queued deploy waits for its turn before failing, in seconds: from 60 (shorter
values are rounded up) to 21600. `0`, the default, means it waits for as long as the
pipeline's timeout allows.


<a id="nestedatt--protection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protection`

Optional:

- `allowed_refs` (List of String) Globs the ref a run was started from must match for it to deploy here, in the same pattern
language as branch rules. Empty allows any ref.
- `prevent_self_approval` (Boolean) Whether the person who started the run is barred from approving its deployment. What counts
is who started the run, not who wrote the commit: deploying somebody else's commit is still
your deploy.
- `required` (Number) Distinct approvals needed before the deployment starts, 1–10.
- `requires_approval` (Boolean) When set, a deployment to this environment waits for approval before it starts. Nothing runs
and no credentials are issued while it waits.
- `wait_timer_seconds` (Number) How long a deployment waits before it may start, in seconds, up to one hour. `0` means no
wait.


<a id="nestedatt--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and environment_id, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_group_catalog_environment.example "<group_id>/<environment_id>"
```
